blocks.orig: Do you want to go scuba diving in Zanzibar? This tropical archipelago in the Indian Ocean that can be found just off the coast of both Kenya and Tanzania features some of the most gorgeous and idyllic beaches and scuba diving sites in the world.
blocks.html: Thinking about scuba diving in Zanzibar? Lying in the Indian Ocean just off the coasts of Kenya and Tanzania, this tropical archipelago has some of the world's loveliest, most idyllic beaches and dive sites.

blocks.orig: The beauty can be found both above and below the glimmering waters of Zanzibar, with various scuba diving sites available in the area that feature a wealth of varied sea life – including more than 500 species of marine life – and an abundance of coral reefs.
blocks.html: In Zanzibar you'll find beauty above the sparkling water as well as beneath it, with a number of local dive sites offering plentiful coral reefs and a rich mix of sea life – more than 500 species of marine life in total.

blocks.orig: There are more than thirty dive sites around Zanzibar – including wreck diving and reef exploration – allowing for a range of diving activities for everyone, from deep divers to snorkelers.
blocks.html: Zanzibar has over thirty dive sites – covering both reef exploration and wreck diving – so there is something for everyone, whether you are a snorkeler or a deep diver.

blocks.orig: With this in mind, we are going to be looking at some of the best scuba diving sites to be found in Zanzibar. We are also going to be taking a look at when the best time to go diving is. Let’s get started.
blocks.html: So below, we'll go through a selection of the best places for scuba diving in Zanzibar, and we'll also look at the ideal time of year to dive. Let’s begin.

blocks.orig: Best Season To Go Scuba Diving In Zanzibar
blocks.html: The best time of year for scuba diving in Zanzibar

blocks.orig: If you want to go scuba diving in Zanzibar during a time when the conditions are more stable, you will find the best time to be in the months of October, November, March, and April.
blocks.html: For scuba diving in Zanzibar when conditions are at their most stable, October, November, March and April are the best months to choose.

blocks.orig: These months tend to have low winds that aren’t strong and calm oceans, which allows you to get the best possible visibility as you dive.
blocks.html: During these months the winds are usually light and aren’t strong, and the sea is calm, which gives you the clearest possible visibility underwater.

blocks.orig: The windy season in Zanzibar occurs in December and January. These strong winds can limit visibility and can lead to limited exploration or even cancellation of your dive altogether.
blocks.html: December and January make up Zanzibar's windy season. The strong winds at this time can reduce visibility, restrict how much you can explore or even lead to your dive being cancelled altogether.

blocks.orig: However, it is important to remember that the rainy season in Zanzibar begins in April, which could affect your diving experience.
blocks.html: Keep in mind, though, that Zanzibar's rainy season starts in April, and this may have an effect on your dives.

blocks.orig: That being said, let’s now get into the diving sites that are some of the best that you will find during your holiday in Zanzibar!
blocks.html: With that covered, let’s move on to some of the finest dive sites you can visit on your Zanzibar holiday!

blocks.orig: Located in the south of Zanzibar – more specifically in the Kizimkazi area – Kungui scuba dive site is best known for offering the chance to swim with dolphins, making it a hot tourist spot.
blocks.html: In the south of Zanzibar – in the Kizimkazi area, to be precise – lies the Kungui scuba dive site, which is a popular spot with visitors mainly because it gives you the chance to swim with dolphins.

blocks.orig: The site can be found around thirty minutes away from Zanzibar via a boat and is perfect for divers of any experience level, whether it is a beginner, intermediate or advanced.
blocks.html: It is roughly thirty minutes from Zanzibar by boat and suits divers of every level, from beginner to intermediate to advanced.

blocks.orig: The shallower area of the dive site features a coral garden that runs at a depth of around 20 meters before it sharply drops off.
blocks.html: In its shallower section there is a coral garden at a depth of about 20 meters, after which the site drops away steeply.

blocks.orig: The shallow area works as a great experience for beginners, whereas the wall of the drop-off is perfect for more advanced divers.
blocks.html: Beginners will enjoy the shallow section, while the drop-off wall is ideal for more advanced divers.

blocks.orig: When it comes to the creatures that you will find in Kungui, there is a wide variety to be spotted, including different kinds of fish – such as scorpion fish – as well as turtles, stingrays, and octopuses.
blocks.html: Kungui has a wide range of creatures to look out for, including octopuses, stingrays, turtles and many types of fish – scorpion fish among them.

blocks.orig: Tumbatu Island can be found in northern Zanzibar and is made up of three separate dive sites: Mwana, Shetani, and Popobawa.
blocks.html: In northern Zanzibar you'll find Tumbatu Island, which has three distinct dive sites: Mwana, Shetani and Popobawa.

blocks.orig: All of these sites feature some of the most beautiful coral gardens in Zanzibar, with a variety of hard and soft corals.
blocks.html: Each of them has some of the loveliest coral gardens in Zanzibar, with a mix of soft and hard corals.

blocks.orig: The reef around these dive sites begins at around 3 meters and drops to about 12 meters in depth, making it great for snorkelers as well as beginner divers.
blocks.html: At these sites the reef starts at roughly 3 meters and goes down to around 12 meters, so it works well for beginner divers and snorkelers alike.

blocks.orig: Amongst all the dive sites found around Tumbatu Island, you will be able to spot octopuses, moray eels, nudibranchs, scorpion fish, leaf fish, and turtles.
blocks.html: Across the dive sites around Tumbatu Island you can see turtles, leaf fish, scorpion fish, nudibranchs, moray eels and octopuses.

blocks.orig: You’ll find Mwana Wa Mwana just to the northwest of Tumbatu Island, and this uniquely named dive spot is great for divers of all experience levels.
blocks.html: Just northwest of Tumbatu Island you’ll come across Mwana Wa Mwana, a dive spot with an unusual name that suits divers of every experience level.

blocks.orig: Mwana Wa Mwana is a terraced coral garden that starts off shallowly, with a depth of only 3 meters. As you go on, the reef slowly descends to 12 meters.
blocks.html: Mwana Wa Mwana is a coral garden laid out in terraces, beginning in shallow water at just 3 meters deep. From there the reef gradually slopes down to 12 meters.

blocks.orig: You will then be met with a sandy bottom that continues to slope, going down to a depth of 18 meters.
blocks.html: Beyond that is a sandy bottom that keeps sloping until it reaches 18 meters.

blocks.orig: Some sea creatures you might encounter in Mwana Wa Mwana include seahorses, sea turtles, nudibranchs, cuttlefish, stingrays, and more.
blocks.html: At Mwana Wa Mwana you may come across stingrays, cuttlefish, nudibranchs, sea turtles, seahorses and other sea creatures.

blocks.orig: Another dive site that can be found to the northwest of Tumbatu Island, Ras Miskitini is a small coral wall with two depth levels.
blocks.html: Ras Miskitini, also located northwest of Tumbatu Island, is a small coral wall with two levels of depth.

blocks.orig: The initial depth starts at around 5 meters and drops to 12 meters. You’ll find some coral bommies before the slope gently descends to around 20 meters.
blocks.html: It begins at roughly 5 meters and drops to 12 meters. You’ll come across a few coral bommies before the slope eases down to about 20 meters.

blocks.orig: An eclectic range of sea life can be spotted here, including Spotwing flying gurnard, sea turtles, leaf scorpion fish, and more.
blocks.html: The marine life here is varied and includes leaf scorpion fish, sea turtles, Spotwing flying gurnard and others.

blocks.orig: Three Turtles can be found underneath both Mwana Wa Mwana and Ras Misikitini and to the west of Tumbatu Island. It is similar to Ras Miskitini in that it is also a small wall coral reef.
blocks.html: Three Turtles lies below both Mwana Wa Mwana and Ras Misikitini, to the west of Tumbatu Island. Like Ras Miskitini, it is a small coral reef wall.

blocks.orig: The depth isn’t quite as deep as Ras Miskitini, though, with an initial drop of 3 to 12 meters that goes further down to 16 meters following a sloping descent.
blocks.html: It isn’t as deep as Ras Miskitini, however: the first drop goes from 3 to 12 meters, followed by a sloping descent down to 16 meters.

blocks.orig: The coral at Three Turtles is known for its bright and vibrant colors, making it a memorable experience for both divers and snorkelers.
blocks.html: Three Turtles is known for its bright, vivid coral, which makes it a memorable dive for snorkelers and divers alike.

blocks.orig: Reef fish are prevalent in Three Turtles, as are stingrays, octopuses, scorpion fish, and sea turtles to name a few.
blocks.html: At Three Turtles you'll find plenty of reef fish, along with sea turtles, scorpion fish, octopuses and stingrays, among others.

blocks.orig: Often thought to host some of the absolute best dive sites in Zanzibar, Mnemba Island can be found in the northeast, being particularly close to the main island.
blocks.html: Lying in the northeast and very close to the main island, Mnemba Island is widely considered home to some of Zanzibar's very best dive sites.

blocks.orig: There are various dive sites to be found on Mnemba Island, but some of the most popular are Big Wall, Kichwani, and Wattabomie.
blocks.html: Mnemba Island has several dive sites, with Big Wall, Kichwani and Wattabomie among the most popular.

blocks.orig: Big Wall is better suited for divers in the intermediate to advanced skill range, as it has a significant depth of 18 meters to more than 35 meters.
blocks.html: With a considerable depth of 18 meters to over 35 meters, Big Wall is more suitable for intermediate to advanced divers.

blocks.orig: The reef within Big Wall is a vertical wall that can be found in the open sea, making it another choice that is better suited to more experienced divers (as does the strength of the current).
blocks.html: The Big Wall reef is a vertical wall out in the open sea, which, together with the strength of the current, makes it a better option for more experienced divers.

blocks.orig: Whilst there aren’t many corals in Big Wall, there are plenty of caves and overhangs that are perfect for exploration.
blocks.html: Big Wall doesn’t have a lot of coral, but it does have lots of overhangs and caves that are ideal for exploring.

blocks.orig: Common sea creatures that can be spotted include tunas, groupers, barracudas, bigeyes, Napoleon wrasses, rainbow runners, and lobsters. Some more occasional sightings include stingrays and white tip reef sharks.
blocks.html: Sea life you'll commonly see includes lobsters, rainbow runners, Napoleon wrasses, bigeyes, barracudas, groupers and tunas. Less frequent sightings include white tip reef sharks and stingrays.

blocks.orig: Kichwani is considered one of the more beautiful dive sites for diving around Mnemba Island, well suited to a range of diving experience levels.
blocks.html: Among the dive sites around Mnemba Island, Kichwani is regarded as one of the prettier ones, and it suits a range of experience levels.

blocks.orig: This sloping wall reef has a depth that ranges from 2 to 30 meters and is covered with both soft and hard corals that harbor a wide variety of sea life.
blocks.html: This sloping reef wall goes from 2 to 30 meters deep and is covered in hard and soft corals that are home to a wide range of marine life.

blocks.orig: These include schools of brightly colored reed fish, leaf fish, scorpion fish, napoleon wrasses, moray eels, trigger fish, and much more (including the occasional white tip reef shark).
blocks.html: You can expect schools of brightly coloured reed fish, trigger fish, moray eels, napoleon wrasses, scorpion fish, leaf fish and plenty more (with the odd white tip reef shark as well).

blocks.orig: A mild current also allows you to drift safely along the wall.
blocks.html: Thanks to a gentle current, you can also drift along the wall safely.

blocks.orig: Wattabomie is another diving experience that is well suited for divers of all experience levels. Wattabomie is a coral reef that can be found on the south of Mnemba Island, reaching around 6 to 30 meters in depth.
blocks.html: Wattabomie is another dive that suits all experience levels. It is a coral reef on the southern side of Mnemba Island, with depths of roughly 6 to 30 meters.

blocks.orig: The reef has a gentle slope, making it perfect for more relaxed diving. The bottom of the reef is unique in that it has a composition that combines beautiful plate coral with incredible bommie coral formations.
blocks.html: Its gentle slope makes it ideal for a more relaxed dive. What makes the bottom of the reef unusual is its mix of lovely plate coral and remarkable bommie coral formations.

blocks.orig: There are various tropical reef fish to be found in the area, as well as king fish, groupers, mantishrimps, snappers, octopuses, Indian Ocean walkmen, barracudas, and more.
blocks.html: The area is home to a variety of tropical reef fish, plus barracudas, Indian Ocean walkmen, octopuses, snappers, mantishrimps, groupers, king fish and more.

blocks.orig: There are even bottlenose dolphins and green turtles to be spotted on occasion!
blocks.html: Now and then you can even see green turtles and bottlenose dolphins!

blocks.orig: Found in the northern Zanzibar dive sites, the Magic Reef is popular with photographer divers due to the beautiful scenery.
blocks.html: Among the dive sites in northern Zanzibar, the Magic Reef is a favourite with underwater photographers thanks to its lovely scenery.

blocks.orig: The reef reaches between 12 and 20 meters and is the perfect spot for those who are most interested in seeing a diverse range of marine life.
blocks.html: Ranging from 12 to 20 meters deep, the reef is ideal if seeing a wide variety of marine life is your main interest.

blocks.orig: Some of the fish and sea life that you will see if you choose the Magic Reef when you dive include seahorses, frog fish, octopuses, turtles, cleaner shrimp, mantis shrimp, crocodile fish, and more.
blocks.html: If you dive the Magic Reef, the fish and sea life you'll see include crocodile fish, mantis shrimp, cleaner shrimp, turtles, octopuses, frog fish, seahorses and more.

blocks.orig: Leven Bank can be found in the far north of Zanzibar, as it is another dive site that is recommended for more experienced and advanced divers due to its position in the middle of the open ocean.
blocks.html: In the far north of Zanzibar lies Leven Bank, another dive site best left to experienced and advanced divers because it sits in the middle of the open ocean.

blocks.orig: This dive site is also a slope that descends drastically, ranging from around 12 meters to 55 meters and having a strong current.
blocks.html: It is also a steeply descending slope, going from about 12 meters down to 55 meters, with a strong current.

blocks.orig: There are plenty of big game fish to be found at Leven Bank – such as tuna and king fish – as well as the likes of moray eels, barracuda, and trevally.
blocks.html: Leven Bank has lots of big game fish – king fish and tuna, for example – along with trevally, barracuda and moray eels.

blocks.orig: You can also find tiny forms of marine life, such as nudibranchs. Large schools of reef fish are also known to populate the area.
blocks.html: Tiny marine life such as nudibranchs can be found here too, and the area is known for its large schools of reef fish.

blocks.orig: As well as that, from August through to September, there is the chance to see some beautiful Humpback Whales.
blocks.html: On top of that, between August and September you have a chance of seeing beautiful Humpback Whales.

blocks.orig: Accessible via a lengthy boat ride from Stone Town – an older area of Zanzibar City (which is the main city within Zanzibar) – the Boribu dive site is full of various, colorful underwater splendors, from spectacular gorgonian sea fans to large barrel sponges, columnar corals and much more!
blocks.html: Reached by a long boat trip from Stone Town – the old part of Zanzibar City (Zanzibar's main city) – the Boribu dive site is packed with colourful underwater sights, from striking gorgonian sea fans to big barrel sponges, columnar corals and plenty more!

blocks.orig: When it comes to what sea creatures you will find during your time diving at Boribu, the area is prone to schools of pelagic fish as well as moral eels and large lobsters.
blocks.html: As for the sea life you'll meet while diving at Boribu, the site tends to attract schools of pelagic fish, as well as moral eels and big lobsters.

blocks.orig: If you visit during the right season, it is also possible to spot a whale shark!
blocks.html: Come at the right time of year and you may even see a whale shark!

blocks.orig: Nungwi can be found on the northeastern tip of Zanzibar, and it is home to various beautiful diving spots, such as Shane’s Reef, Mbwangawa, Kichafi, and more.
blocks.html: On Zanzibar's northeastern tip lies Nungwi, which has several lovely dive spots, including Shane’s Reef, Mbwangawa, Kichafi and others.

blocks.orig: Shane’s Reef is a somewhat unique dive site made up of sandy bottom patches and coral reefs with an initial depth of 10 meters that gently goes down to 14 meters.
blocks.html: Shane’s Reef is a rather unusual dive site, combining coral reefs with sandy patches on the bottom; it starts at 10 meters and gently descends to 14 meters.

blocks.orig: This then slope – again, in a gradual manner – to 20 meters.
blocks.html: From there it slopes down – once more, gradually – to 20 meters.

blocks.orig: Both macro marine life and other sea creatures can be found on Shane’s Reef, such as seahorses, black-botched porcupine fish, weedy scorpion fish, Spotwing flying gurnard, and more.
blocks.html: On Shane’s Reef you can find macro marine life as well as other sea creatures, including Spotwing flying gurnard, weedy scorpion fish, black-botched porcupine fish, seahorses and more.

blocks.orig: Mwabanga is an extensive coral reef that brings together soft and hard corals via two main areas of plate coral formations.
blocks.html: Mwabanga is a large coral reef where hard and soft corals come together across two main areas of plate coral formations.

blocks.orig: The depth begins lightly at 7 meters, with gentle slopes that decrease to 18 meters. The mild current allows for some drift diving as you observe colorful reef fish, stone fish, groupers, stingrays, guitar fish, and more.
blocks.html: It starts at a shallow 7 meters, with gentle slopes going down to 18 meters. Thanks to the mild current, you can do some drift diving while watching guitar fish, stingrays, groupers, stone fish, colourful reef fish and more.

blocks.orig: Another coral reef diving spot, Kichafi, features soft and hard corals that are fringed by unique and colorful plate coral formations as well as colorful sea cabbage.
blocks.html: Kichafi, another coral reef dive spot, has hard and soft corals edged by colourful sea cabbage and distinctive, colourful plate coral formations.

blocks.orig: With a depth of between 10 and 16 meters, it is well suited to a range of experience levels.
blocks.html: At 10 to 16 meters deep, it suits a variety of experience levels.

blocks.orig: If you venture to Kichafi for a late afternoon or early morning dive, you might be able to see some large stingrays, cobias, or mackerels. Otherwise, you’ll find reef fish, parrot fish, and spade fish to name a few.
blocks.html: Dive Kichafi in the early morning or late afternoon and you may see mackerels, cobias or large stingrays. At other times, you’ll see spade fish, parrot fish and reef fish, among others.

blocks.orig: Located underneath Shane’s Reef and to the northwest of Zanzibar, this circular reef is another that is found in the open sea with a depth of 10 to 17 meters.
blocks.html: Lying below Shane’s Reef, northwest of Zanzibar, this round reef is another open-sea site, with depths of 10 to 17 meters.

blocks.orig: Hunga is known for its excellent level of visibility as well as its massive bommies that are covered with a range of bright, colorful corals.
blocks.html: Hunga is known for its very good visibility and its huge bommies, which are covered in a variety of bright, colourful corals.

blocks.orig: Hunga is an excellent mid-water diving experience, with sea life such as redtooth, bat fish, unicorn fish, crocodile fish, and trigger fish being common as well as sightings of spot eagle rays being possible.
blocks.html: Hunga makes for a superb mid-water dive, where trigger fish, crocodile fish, unicorn fish, bat fish and redtooth are common, and you may also see spot eagle rays.

blocks.orig: So there you have some of the best scuba diving spots that you will find in Zanzibar!
blocks.html: Those are some of the best places to go scuba diving in Zanzibar!

blocks.orig: Hopefully, our list has proven that no matter whether your skill level is beginner, intermediate or advanced when it comes to diving, there are tons of options available to you if you are looking to experience a scuba diving adventure in Zanzibar.
blocks.html: We hope our list shows that whether you are a beginner, intermediate or advanced diver, you have lots of choice if you want to enjoy a scuba diving adventure in Zanzibar.
